segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > 스캔, 탭, 태그 읽음 하나하나가 데이터 포인트이고, 현대 소매는 이 포인트들을 '뭘 진열하고, 얼마에 팔고, 언제 재주문할지'에 대한 결정으로 바꾸는 능력에 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: **소매 정보 시스템**은 판매 현장에서 의사결정 담당자까지 데이터를 옮겨 주는 파이프라인입니다.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: 알아 둘 만한 세 가지 층으로 이루어져 있습니다.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS(판매 시점)**는 계산대입니다.

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: 계산원이 시리얼 상자를 스캔하면 바코드의 UPC가 매장의 상품 파일에서 조회되어 상품 설명과 현재 가격을 반환합니다.

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: 그 한 번의 스캔이 여러 작업을 동시에 수행합니다: 상품 가격을 정하고, 판매를 기록하고, 재고 수량을 줄이고, 거래에 타임스탬프를 붙입니다.

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: 이것이 계산대가 가격을 알고 진열 태그는 알 필요가 없는 이유입니다. *가격 조회*라고 불리는 설계이며, U.S.

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: 식료품점에서 1970년대 이후 표준입니다.

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID(무선 주파수 인식)**는 한 걸음 더 나아갑니다.

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: RFID 태그는 작은 칩과 안테나로, 보통 배터리가 없으며, 리더가 거리에서 전원을 공급하고 무선으로 읽습니다.

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: 바코드에 비한 장점: 시선이 필요 없고, 초당 수백 개의 태그를 읽을 수 있으며, 각 태그는 그 특정 단위에 고유한 일련번호를 가집니다. 단순히 "중형 파란색 폴로셔츠"가 아니라 *그 특정한* 중형 파란색 폴로셔츠입니다.

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: 의류 소매상은 재고 확인에 많이 사용합니다. 매장 직원이 휴대용 리더로 매장을 돌아다니며 밤새 들이는 대신 1시간 미만에 전체 매장을 재고 확인할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **소매 빅데이터**는 모든 데이터를 보관할 때 일어나는 것입니다.

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: 전국 규모의 체인점은 연간 수십억 건의 거래 기록을 생성하고, 이를 멤버십 카드 ID, 날씨, 프로모션, 웹 브라우징과 결합하면 분석가들이 단일 매장 관리자는 답할 수 없는 질문에 답할 수 있습니다: 어떤 상품들이 함께 팔리는가, 가격 인상이 실제로 판량을 얼마나 바꾸는가, 이번 주말에 어느 매장이 상품 부족에 직면할 것인가.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: 연결된 개념은 **재고 정확도**입니다. 컴퓨터의 수량과 진열대의 실제 수량이 얼마나 가깝게 일치하는가입니다.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: 소매상은 POS 데이터에만 의존할 때 개별 상품 수준에서 보통 60–80% 범위의 정확도를 발견합니다. 도난, 잘못 진열된 상품, 수령 오류가 모두 조용히 수량을 깨뜨리기 때문입니다.

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: 잘못된 재고 수량은 **품절**(있다고 생각해서 재주문하지 않음)과 과도한 할인(없다고 생각해서 과다주문)을 야기합니다.

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: 이 분야의 거의 모든 것이 그 차이를 줄이기 위해 노력하고 있습니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: 미국의 Target 매장에 들어가

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: $24.99짜리 티셔츠를 집어듭니다.

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: 셔츠에는 내부에 RFID 칩이 라미네이트된 종이 가격 태그가 있습니다.

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: 밤새 또는 한가한 시간에 직원이 휴대용 리더로 부서를 훑고 모든 태그를 집어듭니다. 고객이 양말 코너에 던져둔 셔츠 3개를 포함해서요. 시스템은 이를 "재고 있음"으로 계산했지만 쇼핑객은 절대 찾을 수 없는 것들입니다.

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: 그것이 **가상 품절**입니다: 컴퓨터는 있다고 하지만 고객은 없다고 하는 재고입니다.

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: 계산대에서 바코드 스캔이 셔츠를 보유 재고에서 제거하고, Target Circle 앱을 스캔했다면 구매를 당신의 가정과 연결합니다.

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: 그 기록은 여러 시스템에 병렬로 공급됩니다: 보충 시스템이 시카고 물류 센터가 이 매장에 중형을 더 배송할지 결정합니다. 가격 책정팀은 프로모션이 실제로 판량을 올렸는지, 아니면 정가를 낼 사람들에게만 할인을 준 것인지 봅니다. 개인화 엔진은 다음주에 받을 쿠폰의 카테고리를 기록합니다.

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: 같은 기반 시설이 온라인 구매-매장 픽업을 지원합니다.

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: 웹사이트가 "2시간 안에 준비"라고 약속할 때, 매장의 재고 기록이 정확하다고 내기하는 것입니다.

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: 수량이 잘못되면 주문이 몇 시간 후 취소되고 고객의 신뢰에 타격을 입습니다. 이것이 정확히 체인점들이 효율성이 나오는 카테고리에서 RFID에 큰 투자를 하는 이유입니다.

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: 한 가지 솔직한 주의사항: RFID 태그의 비용은 대략 각각 몇 센트이고, 리더와 소프트웨어는 별도입니다.

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: 수백 가지 사이즈-색상 조합이 있는 $25짜리 셔츠에는 정당화하기 쉽지만, 99센트짜리 수프 캔에는 정당화하기 어렵습니다.

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: 이것이 의류가 먼저 채택하고 식료품점이 대부분 아직 채택하지 않은 이유입니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. POS turns each checkout into a priced, timestamped, inventory-adjusting record — the base layer of all retail data.
segments.tr: 1. POS는 각 계산을 가격이 정해지고, 타임스탬프가 붙고, 재고가 조정된 기록으로 바꿉니다. 모든 소매 데이터의 기초 층입니다.

segments.src: 2. RFID adds item-level, no-line-of-sight visibility, which mainly buys you inventory accuracy and therefore fewer out-of-stocks.
segments.tr: 2. RFID는 상품 수준의 시선 불필요한 가시성을 추가합니다. 이는 주로 재고 정확도를 확보하고 따라서 품절을 줄입니다.

segments.src: 3. Big data is the payoff layer: combining transactions with customer, price, and context data to decide what to stock, charge, and promote.
segments.tr: 3. 빅데이터는 보상 층입니다: 거래를 고객, 가격, 상황 데이터와 결합하여 뭘 진열하고, 얼마에 팔고, 뭘 홍보할지 결정합니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 평가

segments.src: **1.** In a standard U.S.
supermarket POS system, where does the price of a scanned item come from?
segments.tr: 식료품점 POS 시스템에서 스캔된 상품의 가격은 어디서 옵니까?

segments.src: - (a) It's encoded in the barcode itself
segments.tr: - (a) 바코드 자체에 인코딩됨

segments.src: - (b) A price look-up in the store's item file, keyed by the UPC
segments.tr: - (b) 매장의 상품 파일에서 UPC를 키로 하는 가격 조회

segments.src: - (c) The cashier types it in from the shelf tag
segments.tr: - (c) 계산원이 진열 태그에서 입력함

segments.src: - (d) The manufacturer transmits it at checkout
segments.tr: - (d) 제조업체가 계산 시 전송함

segments.src: **2.** True or False: An RFID tag must be visible to the reader, in a straight line, to be scanned.
segments.tr: **2.** 참 또는 거짓: RFID 태그가 스캔되려면 리더에 보여야 하고, 직선으로 있어야 합니다.

segments.src: **3.** A store's system says 6 units are on hand, but a customer can't find any on the shelf because they were misshelved in another aisle.
segments.tr: **3.** 매장 시스템이 6개가 보유 중이라고 하지만, 고객은 진열대에서 아무것도 찾을 수 없습니다. 다른 코너에 잘못 진열되었기 때문입니다.

segments.src: This is best described as:
segments.tr: 이것은 가장 잘 설명된 것이:

segments.src: - (a) Shrinkage
segments.tr: - (a) 손실

segments.src: - (b) A phantom out-of-stock
segments.tr: - (b) 가상 품절

segments.src: - (c) A markdown
segments.tr: - (c) 할인

segments.src: - (d) A stockout at the distribution center
segments.tr: - (d) 물류 센터에서의 품절

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **POS (point of sale):** The system at checkout that prices items, captures the transaction, and updates inventory in one step.
segments.tr: - **POS(판매 시점):** 계산대의 시스템으로 상품 가격을 정하고, 거래를 캡처하고, 재고를 한 단계에서 업데이트합니다.

segments.src: - **UPC / barcode:** A printed code identifying a product type; it's a key into a database, not a container of price information.
segments.tr: - **UPC/바코드:** 상품 유형을 식별하는 인쇄된 코드. 데이터베이스의 키이지 가격 정보의 컨테이너가 아닙니다.

segments.src: - **RFID:** Wireless tag-and-reader technology that identifies individual items without line of sight, at high speed.
segments.tr: - **RFID:** 시선 불필요하게 개별 상품을 고속으로 식별하는 무선 태그-리더 기술.

segments.src: - **Inventory accuracy:** The match rate between recorded on-hand quantity and actual physical quantity, measured per item.
segments.tr: - **재고 정확도:** 기록된 보유 수량과 실제 물리적 수량 간의 일치율, 상품당 측정.

segments.src: - **Out-of-stock (OOS):** A product a customer wants to buy but can't find available; "phantom" OOS means the system wrongly believes it's in stock.
segments.tr: - **품절(OOS):** 고객이 구매하고 싶지만 사용 가능한 것을 찾을 수 없는 상품. "가상" OOS는 시스템이 잘못해서 재고가 있다고 믿는 것을 의미합니다.

segments.src: - **Shrinkage:** Inventory lost to theft, damage, or error — a main reason recorded counts drift away from reality.
segments.tr: - **손실:** 도난, 손상, 오류로 인한 재고 손실. 기록된 수량이 현실에서 벗어나는 주요 이유입니다.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS（销售点）**是收银机。

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: 当收银员扫描一盒谷物麦片时，条形码的UPC在商店的商品文件中查询，返回描述和当前价格。

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: 那一次扫描同时完成几项工作：为商品定价、记录销售、减少现有库存计数，并为交易添加时间戳。

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么收银机知道价格而货架标签不需要知道的原因——一种称为*价格查询*的设计，在美国

segments.tr: 杂货店自1970年代以来就是标准做法。

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID（射频识别）**更进一步。

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: RFID标签是一个微小的芯片和天线，通常没有电池，读取器可以从远处为其供电并无线读取。

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: 相比条形码的优势：不需要视线，每秒可读取数百个标签，每个标签携带该特定单位独有的序列号——不仅仅是"M码蓝色Polo衫"，而是*那一件*M码蓝色Polo衫。

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: 服装零售商大量使用它进行库存计数；商店员工可以拿着手持读取器走遍楼层，在不到一小时内清点整个商店，而不是整个晚上。

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **零售大数据**是当你保留所有数据时发生的情况。

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: 一个全国连锁店每年产生数十亿条交易记录，将这些数据与忠诚卡ID、天气、促销和网络浏览数据结合起来，让分析师能够回答单个店长无法回答的问题：哪些产品一起销售，价格变化实际上能推动多少销量，哪家门店本周末即将缺货。

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: 连接的概念是**库存准确性**——电脑中的数字与货架上的数字匹配的程度。

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: 当零售商仅依赖POS数据时，他们通常在个项目级别发现60–80%范围内的准确性，因为盗窃、物品错误放置和收货错误都会无声地破坏计数。

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: 错误的计数导致**缺货**（你以为有货，所以你不补货）和过度降价（你以为没货，所以你过度订购）。

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: 这个领域的几乎所有东西都旨在缩小这个差距。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: 走进美国的一家Target门店

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: 并拿起一件$24.99的T恤。

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: 这件T恤有一个纸质价格标签，内部层压了一个RFID芯片。

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: 一夜之间，或在清闲班次中，一名员工用手持读取器扫过整个部门并拿起每个标签——包括顾客扔在袜子过道的三件T恤，系统计算为"库存中"但没有购物者会找到的。

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: 那是一个**虚拟缺货**：电脑说你有库存，但顾客说你没有。

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: 在收银时，条形码扫描将T恤从现有库存中删除，如果你扫描了Target Circle应用程序，则将购买与你的家庭关联。

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: 该记录并行馈送到多个系统：补货系统决定芝加哥配送中心是否向该商店运送更多M码商品；定价团队看到促销是否真的提升了销量或只是给本来愿意全价支付的人打折；个性化引擎记录下周要发送给你的优惠券的类别。

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: 相同的基础设施支持在线购买门店自提。

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: 当网站承诺"2小时内准备好"时，它是在赌商店的库存记录是正确的。

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: 如果计数错误，订单会在几小时后被取消，顾客的信任会受到打击——这正是为什么连锁店在那些经济上可行的类别中花费了这么多RFID投资。

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: 一个诚实的注意事项：RFID标签每个成本大约几美分，加上读取器和软件。

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: 这很容易在有数百种尺码颜色组合的$25 T恤上证明，但很难在99美分的罐头汤上证明。

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么服装首先采用它而杂货店大多没有。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. POS turns each checkout into a priced, timestamped, inventory-adjusting record — the base layer of all retail data.
segments.tr: 1. POS将每次结账转变为一个定价、加时间戳、调整库存的记录——所有零售数据的基层。

segments.src: 2. RFID adds item-level, no-line-of-sight visibility, which mainly buys you inventory accuracy and therefore fewer out-of-stocks.
segments.tr: 2. RFID增加了项目级、无需视线的可见性，主要为你提供库存准确性，从而减少缺货。

segments.src: 3. Big data is the payoff layer: combining transactions with customer, price, and context data to decide what to stock, charge, and promote.
segments.tr: 3. 大数据是回报层：将交易与顾客、价格和背景数据结合起来，决定库存、定价和促销内容。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **POS (point of sale):** The system at checkout that prices items, captures the transaction, and updates inventory in one step.
segments.tr: - **POS（销售点）：** 结账时的系统，对商品定价、捕获交易并一步更新库存。

segments.src: - **UPC / barcode:** A printed code identifying a product type; it's a key into a database, not a container of price information.
segments.tr: - **UPC /条形码：** 标识产品类型的打印代码；它是进入数据库的钥匙，而不是价格信息的容器。

segments.src: - **RFID:** Wireless tag-and-reader technology that identifies individual items without line of sight, at high speed.
segments.tr: - **RFID：** 无线标签和读取器技术，可在高速下识别单个项目而无需视线。

segments.src: - **Inventory accuracy:** The match rate between recorded on-hand quantity and actual physical quantity, measured per item.
segments.tr: - **库存准确性：** 记录的现有数量和实际物理数量之间的匹配率，按项目衡量。

segments.src: - **Out-of-stock (OOS):** A product a customer wants to buy but can't find available; "phantom" OOS means the system wrongly believes it's in stock.
segments.tr: - **缺货 (OOS)：** 顾客想购买但找不到的产品；"虚拟" OOS 意味着系统错误地认为它有库存。

segments.src: - **Shrinkage:** Inventory lost to theft, damage, or error — a main reason recorded counts drift away from reality.
segments.tr: - **库存缩水：** 因盗窃、损伤或错误而丧失的库存——记录计数与现实偏离的主要原因。

hi.title: [Retailing 101 #14] पूरी दुकान को चलाने वाली चेकआउट बीप

segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > प्रत्येक स्कैन, टैप, और टैग रीड एक डेटा बिंदु है — और आधुनिक खुदरा इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि कोई श्रृंखला इन बिंदुओं को कितनी अच्छी तरह स्टॉक, कीमत, और पुनः ऑर्डर करने के बारे में निर्णयों में बदलती है।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: एक **खुदरा सूचना प्रणाली** वह बुनियादी ढांचा है जो डेटा को बिक्री मंजिल से निर्णय लेने वाले लोगों तक ले जाता है।

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: इसकी तीन परतें जानने योग्य हैं।

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS (बिक्री बिंदु)** रजिस्टर है।

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: जब कोई कैशियर अनाज का एक डिब्बा स्कैन करता है, तो बारकोड का UPC स्टोर की आइटम फ़ाइल में देखा जाता है, जो विवरण और वर्तमान कीमत लौटाता है।

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: यह एक स्कैन एक बार में कई काम करता है: यह आइटम को कीमत देता है, बिक्री रिकॉर्ड करता है, हाथ पर इन्वेंटरी की गणना को कम करता है, और लेनदेन को टाइमस्टैम्प करता है।

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि रजिस्टर कीमत जानता है और शेल्फ टैग को नहीं करना पड़ता — एक डिजाइन जिसे *मूल्य खोज* कहा जाता है, यू.एस. में मानक।

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: किराने की दुकान में 1970 के दशक से।

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID (रेडियो फ्रीक्वेंसी पहचान)** एक कदम आगे जाता है।

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: एक RFID टैग एक छोटी चिप और एंटीना है, आमतौर पर बिना बैटरी के, जिसे एक रीडर दूरी से सक्रिय करता है और वायरलेस रूप से पढ़ता है।

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: बारकोड पर लाभ: कोई दृष्टि रेखा की आवश्यकता नहीं, प्रति सेकंड सैकड़ों टैग पढ़े जाते हैं, और प्रत्येक टैग उस विशिष्ट इकाई के लिए अद्वितीय एक क्रमांक रखता है — केवल "आकार M नीली पोलो" नहीं बल्कि *वह एक* आकार M नीली पोलो।

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: परिधान खुदरा विक्रेता इन्वेंटरी गणना के लिए इसका भारी उपयोग करते हैं; एक स्टोर कर्मचारी एक हैंडहेल्ड रीडर के साथ फर्श पर चल सकता है और पूरी रात की जगह एक घंटे में पूरे स्टोर की गणना कर सकता है।

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **खुदरा बिग डेटा** वह है जो तब होता है जब आप इसे सब कुछ रखते हैं।

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: एक राष्ट्रीय श्रृंखला एक वर्ष में अरबों लेनदेन लाइनें उत्पन्न करती है, और उन्हें वफादारी-कार्ड आईडी, मौसम, प्रचार, और वेब ब्राउजिंग के साथ जोड़ना विश्लेषकों को ऐसे प्रश्नों का उत्तर देने देता है जो एक एकल स्टोर मैनेजर नहीं कर सकता: कौन सी उत्पादें एक साथ बेचते हैं, कीमत परिवर्तन वास्तव में कितनी मात्रा चलाता है, कौन सा स्टोर इस सप्ताहांत एक आइटम से बाहर होने वाला है।

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: जोड़ने वाला विचार **इन्वेंटरी सटीकता** है — कंप्यूटर में संख्या शेल्फ पर संख्या से कितनी करीब मेल खाती है।

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: खुदरा विक्रेता नियमित रूप से व्यक्तिगत वस्तु स्तर पर 60–80% रेंज में सटीकता पाते हैं जब वे केवल POS डेटा पर निर्भर करते हैं, क्योंकि चोरी, गलत जगह की वस्तुएं, और प्राप्त करने में त्रुटियां सभी चुप से गणना को तोड़ देती हैं।

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: खराब गणना **स्टॉक समाप्ति** (आप सोचते हैं कि आपके पास है, इसलिए आप पुनः ऑर्डर नहीं करते) और अतिरिक्त मार्कडाउन (आप सोचते हैं कि आप खत्म हो गए, इसलिए आप अधिक ऑर्डर करते) का कारण बनती है।

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: इस क्षेत्र में लगभग सब कुछ उस अंतर को बंद करने के लिए लक्षित है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: यू.एस. में एक Target में चलें।

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: और एक $24.99 टी-शर्ट उठाएं।

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: शर्ट में एक कागज की कीमत टैग है जिसमें अंदर एक RFID चिप लैमिनेट की गई है।

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: रातोंरात, या एक धीमी पारी के दौरान, एक कर्मचारी एक हैंडहेल्ड रीडर के साथ विभाग को स्कैन करता है और हर टैग उठाता है — जिसमें तीन शर्ट शामिल हैं जो एक ग्राहक ने मोजे की गली में फेंकी थीं, जिसे सिस्टम ने "स्टॉक में" गिना था लेकिन कोई खरीदार कभी नहीं खोज सकता था।

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: यह एक **फैंटम स्टॉक समाप्ति** है: इन्वेंटरी जो कंप्यूटर कहता है कि आपके पास है और ग्राहक कहता है कि आपके पास नहीं है।

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: चेकआउट पर, बारकोड स्कैन शर्ट को हाथ पर इन्वेंटरी से बाहर निकालता है और, यदि आपने Target Circle ऐप को स्कैन किया है, तो खरीद को आपके घर से जोड़ता है।

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: वह रिकॉर्ड समानांतर में कई प्रणालियों को खिलाता है: पुनःपूर्ति तय करती है कि क्या शिकागो में वितरण केंद्र इस स्टोर को अधिक मध्यम भेजता है; मूल्य निर्धारण टीम देखती है कि क्या प्रचार वास्तव में इकाइयों को बढ़ाया गया या सिर्फ उन लोगों को छूट दी गई जो पूरी कीमत देते; और व्यक्तिगतकरण इंजन अगले सप्ताह मिलने वाले कूपन के लिए श्रेणी को नोट करता है।

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: एक ही बुनियादी ढांचा ऑनलाइन-खरीदें-इन-स्टोर-पिकअप को शक्ति देता है।

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: जब वेबसाइट "2 घंटे में तैयार" का वादा करती है, तो यह स्टोर के इन्वेंटरी रिकॉर्ड के सही होने पर दांव लगा रही है।

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: यदि गणना गलत है, तो ऑर्डर घंटों बाद रद्द कर दिया जाता है और ग्राहक का विश्वास प्रभावित होता है — यही कारण है कि श्रृंखलाएं उन श्रेणियों के लिए RFID पर इतना खर्च करती हैं जहां यह काम करता है।

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: एक ईमानदार चेतावनी: RFID टैग प्रत्येक में लगभग कुछ सेंट की लागत, साथ ही रीडर और सॉफ्टवेयर।

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: यह एक $25 शर्ट पर सैकड़ों आकार-रंग संयोजन के साथ सही ठहराना आसान है, और 99-सेंट सूप के डिब्बे पर सही ठहराना कठिन है।

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि परिधान ने इसे पहले अपनाया और किराने की दुकान ने ज्यादातर नहीं किया।

segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. POS turns each checkout into a priced, timestamped, inventory-adjusting record — the base layer of all retail data.
segments.tr: 1. POS प्रत्येक चेकआउट को एक मूल्य-निर्धारित, टाइमस्टैम्प किया गया, इन्वेंटरी-समायोजन रिकॉर्ड में बदलता है — सभी खुदरा डेटा की आधार परत।

segments.src: 2. RFID adds item-level, no-line-of-sight visibility, which mainly buys you inventory accuracy and therefore fewer out-of-stocks.
segments.tr: 2. RFID आइटम-स्तर, दृष्टि-रेखा-रहित दृश्यमानता जोड़ता है, जो मुख्य रूप से आपको इन्वेंटरी सटीकता और इसलिए कम स्टॉक समाप्ति खरीदता है।

segments.src: 3. Big data is the payoff layer: combining transactions with customer, price, and context data to decide what to stock, charge, and promote.
segments.tr: 3. बिग डेटा भुगतान परत है: स्टॉक, चार्ज, और प्रचार करने के लिए क्या निर्णय लेने के लिए ग्राहक, कीमत, और संदर्भ डेटा के साथ लेनदेन को जोड़ना।

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **POS (point of sale):** The system at checkout that prices items, captures the transaction, and updates inventory in one step.
segments.tr: - **POS (बिक्री बिंदु):** चेकआउट पर प्रणाली जो आइटम को मूल्य देती है, लेनदेन को कैप्चर करती है, और एक कदम में इन्वेंटरी को अपडेट करती है।

segments.src: - **UPC / barcode:** A printed code identifying a product type; it's a key into a database, not a container of price information.
segments.tr: - **UPC / बारकोड:** एक प्रिंट किया गया कोड जो एक उत्पाद प्रकार की पहचान करता है; यह एक डेटाबेस में एक कुंजी है, कीमत जानकारी का एक कंटेनर नहीं है।

segments.src: - **RFID:** Wireless tag-and-reader technology that identifies individual items without line of sight, at high speed.
segments.tr: - **RFID:** वायरलेस टैग-और-रीडर तकनीक जो व्यक्तिगत वस्तुओं की पहचान करती है दृष्टि रेखा के बिना, उच्च गति पर।

segments.src: - **Inventory accuracy:** The match rate between recorded on-hand quantity and actual physical quantity, measured per item.
segments.tr: - **इन्वेंटरी सटीकता:** रिकॉर्ड किए गए हाथ पर मात्रा और वास्तविक भौतिक मात्रा के बीच मेल की दर, प्रति वस्तु मापी जाती है।

segments.src: - **Out-of-stock (OOS):** A product a customer wants to buy but can't find available; "phantom" OOS means the system wrongly believes it's in stock.
segments.tr: - **स्टॉक समाप्ति (OOS):** एक उत्पाद जो एक ग्राहक खरीदना चाहता है लेकिन उपलब्ध नहीं खोज सकता; "फैंटम" OOS का मतलब है कि सिस्टम गलत तरीके से मानता है कि यह स्टॉक में है।

segments.src: - **Shrinkage:** Inventory lost to theft, damage, or error — a main reason recorded counts drift away from reality.
segments.tr: - **सिकुड़न:** चोरी, नुकसान, या त्रुटि के लिए खोई हुई इन्वेंटरी — रिकॉर्ड की गई गणना वास्तविकता से दूर जाने का एक मुख्य कारण।

es.title: [Retailing 101 #14] El Beep del Checkout Que Dirige Toda la Tienda

segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > Cada escaneo, toque y lectura de etiqueta es un punto de datos — y el comercio minorista moderno funciona según cuán bien una cadena convierte esos puntos en decisiones sobre qué surtir, fijar precios y reordenar.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: Un **sistema de información minorista** es la infraestructura que mueve datos del piso de ventas a las personas que toman decisiones.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: Tiene tres capas que vale la pena conocer.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS (punto de venta)** es la caja registradora.

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: Cuando un cajero escanea una caja de cereales, el UPC del código de barras se busca en el archivo de artículos de la tienda, que devuelve la descripción y el precio actual.

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: Ese único escaneo realiza varios trabajos a la vez: establece el precio del artículo, registra la venta, reduce el conteo de inventario disponible y marca la hora de la transacción.

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: Por eso la caja registradora conoce el precio y la etiqueta del estante no tiene que hacerlo — un diseño llamado *búsqueda de precio*, estándar en EE.UU.

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: de comestibles desde los años 70.

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID (identificación por radiofrecuencia)** va un paso más allá.

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: Una etiqueta RFID es un pequeño chip y antena, generalmente sin batería, que un lector activa desde la distancia y lee de forma inalámbrica.

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: Las ventajas sobre los códigos de barras: no se necesita línea de vista, cientos de etiquetas leídas por segundo, y cada etiqueta lleva un número de serie único para esa unidad específica — no solo "polo azul talla M" sino *ese* polo azul talla M.

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: Los minoristas de ropa la usan ampliamente para conteos de inventario; un empleado de la tienda puede caminar por el piso con un lector de mano y contar toda la tienda en menos de una hora en lugar de una noche completa.

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **Big data minorista** es lo que sucede cuando guardas todo.

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: Una cadena nacional genera miles de millones de líneas de transacción al año, y combinar esas con IDs de tarjeta de lealtad, clima, promociones y navegación web permite a los analistas responder preguntas que un único gerente de tienda no puede: qué productos se venden juntos, cuánto un cambio de precio realmente mueve volumen, cuál tienda está a punto de agotar un artículo este fin de semana.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: La idea conectora es **precisión del inventario** — cuán estrechamente el número en la computadora coincide con el número en el estante.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: Los minoristas encuentran rutinariamente precisión en el rango del 60-80% a nivel de artículo individual cuando se basan únicamente en datos de POS, porque el robo, los artículos mal colocados y los errores de recepción rompen el conteo silenciosamente.

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: Los conteos incorrectos causan **falta de existencias** (crees que lo tienes, así que no reordenas) y descuentos excesivos (crees que se acabó, así que ordenas en exceso).

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: Casi todo en este campo tiene como objetivo cerrar esa brecha.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: Entra a una Target en los EE.UU.

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: y recoge una camiseta de $24.99.

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: La camiseta tiene una etiqueta de precio de papel con un chip RFID laminado adentro.

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: Durante la noche, o durante un turno lento, un empleado barre el departamento con un lector de mano y recoge cada etiqueta — incluyendo las tres camisetas que un cliente tiró en el pasillo de calcetines, que el sistema había contado como "en stock" pero que ningún comprador encontraría nunca.

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: Eso es una **falta de existencias fantasma**: inventario que la computadora dice que tienes y el cliente dice que no tienes.

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: En el pago, el escaneo del código de barras saca la camiseta del inventario disponible y, si escaneaste la aplicación Target Circle, vincula la compra a tu hogar.

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: Ese registro alimenta varios sistemas en paralelo: reabastecimiento decide si el centro de distribución en Chicago envía más medidas a esta tienda; el equipo de precios ve si la promoción realmente elevó unidades o solo dio un descuento a personas que hubieran pagado el precio completo; y el motor de personalización anota la categoría para los cupones que recibes la próxima semana.

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: La misma infraestructura impulsa compra en línea, recoge en tienda.

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: Cuando el sitio web promete "Listo en 2 horas", está apostando a que el registro de inventario de la tienda sea correcto.

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: Si el conteo es incorrecto, el pedido se cancela horas después y la confianza del cliente se ve afectada — que es precisamente por qué las cadenas han gastado tanto en RFID para las categorías donde tiene sentido económico.

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: Una advertencia honesta: las etiquetas RFID cuestan aproximadamente algunos centavos cada una, más lectores y software.

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: Eso es fácil de justificar en una camiseta de $25 con cientos de combinaciones de tamaño-color, y difícil de justificar en una lata de sopa de 99 centavos.

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: Por eso la ropa la adoptó primero y los comestibles en su mayoría no.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary

segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **POS (point of sale):** The system at checkout that prices items, captures the transaction, and updates inventory in one step.
segments.tr: - **POS (punto de venta):** El sistema en el pago que establece precios de artículos, captura la transacción y actualiza el inventario en un paso.

segments.src: - **UPC / barcode:** A printed code identifying a product type; it's a key into a database, not a container of price information.
segments.tr: - **UPC / código de barras:** Un código impreso que identifica un tipo de producto; es una clave en una base de datos, no un contenedor de información de precio.

segments.src: - **RFID:** Wireless tag-and-reader technology that identifies individual items without line of sight, at high speed.
segments.tr: - **RFID:** Tecnología inalámbrica de etiqueta y lector que identifica artículos individuales sin línea de vista, a alta velocidad.

segments.src: - **Inventory accuracy:** The match rate between recorded on-hand quantity and actual physical quantity, measured per item.
segments.tr: - **Precisión del inventario:** La tasa de coincidencia entre la cantidad registrada disponible y la cantidad física real, medida por artículo.

segments.src: - **Out-of-stock (OOS):** A product a customer wants to buy but can't find available; "phantom" OOS means the system wrongly believes it's in stock.
segments.tr: - **Falta de existencias (OOS):** Un producto que un cliente quiere comprar pero no puede encontrar disponible; OOS "fantasma" significa que el sistema cree erróneamente que está en stock.

segments.src: - **Shrinkage:** Inventory lost to theft, damage, or error — a main reason recorded counts drift away from reality.
segments.tr: - **Merma:** Inventario perdido por robo, daño o error — una razón principal por la que los conteos registrados se alejan de la realidad.

ar.title: [بيع بالتجزئة 101 #14] الصوت الذي يدير المتجر بأكمله

segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > كل مسح ضوئي وحنة وقراءة وسم هي نقطة بيانات — والبيع بالتجزئة الحديث يعمل على مدى جودة قيام السلسلة بتحويل تلك النقاط إلى قرارات حول ما يجب تخزينه وتسعيره وإعادة طلبه.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## مفهوم اليوم

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: نظام معلومات **البيع بالتجزئة** هو البنية الأساسية التي تنقل البيانات من مكان البيع إلى الأشخاص الذين يتخذون القرارات.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: لها ثلاث طبقات تستحق المعرفة.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **نقطة البيع (POS)** هي أجهزة الكاشير.

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: عندما يقوم أمين الصندوق بمسح صندوق الحبوب ضوئياً، يتم البحث عن رمز UPC للرمز الشريطي في ملف العناصر بالمتجر، والذي يعيد الوصف والسعر الحالي.

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: يقوم هذا المسح الواحد بعدة مهام في وقت واحد: فهو يسعّر العنصر، ويسجل البيع، وينقص عدد المخزون في متناول اليد، ويضع طابع زمني للمعاملة.

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: هذا هو السبب في أن جهاز الكاشير يعرف السعر ولا يتعين على بطاقة الرف — تصميم يسمى *البحث عن السعر*، معيار في الولايات المتحدة.

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: البقالة منذ السبعينيات.

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **تحديد التردد الراديوي (RFID)** تذهب خطوة أبعد.

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: وسم RFID عبارة عن شريحة صغيرة وهوائي، عادة بدون بطارية، يقوم القارئ بتشغيله من بعيد ويقرأه لاسلكياً.

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: المزايا على الرموز الشريطية: لا حاجة لخط البصر، ومئات الوسوم تُقرأ في الثانية الواحدة، وكل وسم يحمل رقم سلسلة فريد لتلك الوحدة المحددة — ليس فقط "حجم M بولو أزرق" بل *هذا* الحجم M بولو أزرق.

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: يستخدم تجار الملابس بكثافة لحسابات المخزون؛ يمكن لموظف المتجر المشي عبر الأرضية بقارئ محمول عد المتجر بأكمله في أقل من ساعة بدلاً من ليلة كاملة.

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **البيانات الضخمة للبيع بالتجزئة** هي ما يحدث عندما تحتفظ بكل ذلك.

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: تولد سلسلة وطنية مليارات أسطر المعاملات في السنة، والجمع بينها وبين معرّفات بطاقات الولاء والطقس والعروض الترويجية والتصفح على الويب يسمح للمحللين بالإجابة على أسئلة لا يمكن لمديري متجر واحد الإجابة عليها: أي المنتجات تُباع معاً، كم يحرك تغيير السعر الحجم فعلياً، أي متجر على وشك نفاد عنصر هذا الأسبوع.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: الفكرة الرابطة هي **دقة المخزون** — مدى قرب الرقم في الكمبيوتر من الرقم على الرف.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: يجد تجار التجزئة بشكل روتيني دقة في نطاق 60–80٪ على مستوى العنصر الفردي عندما يعتمدون على بيانات POS وحدها، لأن السرقة والعناصر الضائعة وأخطاء الاستقبال كلها تكسر العد بصمت.

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: تسبب الأعداد السيئة **نفاد المخزون** (تعتقد أن لديك، لذلك لا تعيد الطلب) والخصومات الزائدة (تعتقد أنك خارج المخزون، لذلك تطلب بكثرة).

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: يهدف كل شيء تقريباً في هذا المجال إلى سد تلك الفجوة.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: ادخل متجر Target في الولايات المتحدة

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: واختر قميص بـ $24.99.

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: القميص له بطاقة سعر ورقية مع شريحة RFID مغلفة بالداخل.

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: خلال الليل، أو أثناء الورديةالبطيئة، يقوم موظف بكنس القسم بقارئ محمول واختيار كل وسم — بما في ذلك قمصان الثلاثة التي ألقاها العميل في ممر الجوارب، والتي عدها النظام على أنها "مخزون" لكن لا أحد من المتسوقين سيجدها أبداً.

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: هذا **نفاد مخزون وهمي**: مخزون يقول الكمبيوتر أن لديك والعميل يقول أنك لا تملك.

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: عند الدفع، يسقط المسح الضوئي للرمز الشريطي القميص من المخزون في متناول اليد، وإذا قمت بمسح تطبيق Target Circle، يربط الشراء بأسرتك.

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: يغذي هذا السجل عدة أنظمة بالتوازي: تقرر إعادة التموين ما إذا كان مركز التوزيع في شيكاغو يشحن المزيد من المقاسات الوسيطة إلى هذا المتجر؛ ترى فريق التسعير ما إذا كان العرض الترويجي فعلاً رفع الوحدات أو مجرد إعطاء خصم للأشخاص الذين كانوا سيدفعون السعر الكامل؛ وتلاحظ محرك التخصيص الفئة للقسائم التي تحصل عليها الأسبوع القادم.

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: نفس البنية الأساسية تشغل الشراء عبر الإنترنت والالتقاط في المتجر.

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: عندما يعد الموقع "جاهز في ساعتين،" فإنه يراهن على أن سجل مخزون المتجر صحيح.

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: إذا كان العد خاطئاً، يتم إلغاء الطلب بعد ساعات والثقة في العميل تأخذ الضربة — وهذا هو السبب بالضبط الذي جعل السلاسل تنفق الكثير على RFID للفئات حيث تستحق التكلفة.

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: تحذير واحد صادق: وسوم RFID تكلف تقريباً عدة سنتات لكل منها، بالإضافة إلى القارئات والبرامج.

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: من السهل تبرير ذلك على قميص بـ $25 مع مئات من مجموعات الحجم واللون، ومن الصعب تبرير ذلك على علبة حساء بـ 99 سنت.

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: هذا هو السبب في أن الملابس اعتمدتها أولاً والبقالة لم تعتمدها في الغالب.

segments.tr: ## ملخص ثلاثة أسطر

fr.title: [Vente au Détail 101 #14] Le Bip de Caisse qui Gère Tout le Magasin

segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > Chaque scan, appui et lecture de balise est un point de données — et le commerce de détail moderne repose sur la capacité d'une chaîne à transformer ces points en décisions concernant ce qu'il faut stocker, à quel prix et quoi réapprovisionner.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept d'Aujourd'hui

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: Un **système d'information de détail** est l'infrastructure qui transporte les données du plancher de vente aux décideurs.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: Il a trois niveaux à connaître.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS (point de vente)** est le registre de caisse.

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: Quand un caissier scanne une boîte de céréales, le code UPC du code-barres est recherché dans le fichier d'articles du magasin, qui retourne la description et le prix actuel.

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: Ce seul scan effectue plusieurs tâches à la fois : il établit le prix de l'article, enregistre la vente, décrémente le compte d'inventaire en stock, et horodate la transaction.

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi le registre connaît le prix et l'étiquette d'étagère ne doit pas — une conception appelée *recherche de prix*, standard aux États-Unis

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: en épicerie depuis les années 1970.

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID (identification par radiofréquence)** va plus loin.

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: Une balise RFID est une minuscule puce et antenne, généralement sans batterie, qu'un lecteur alimente à distance et lit sans fil.

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: Les avantages par rapport aux codes-barres : pas besoin de ligne de vue, des centaines de balises lues par seconde, et chaque balise porte un numéro de série unique à cette unité — pas seulement « polo bleu taille M » mais *ce* polo bleu taille M.

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: Les détaillants de vêtements l'utilisent beaucoup pour les comptages d'inventaire ; un associé peut parcourir le plancher avec un lecteur portatif et compter tout le magasin en moins d'une heure au lieu d'une nuit complète.

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **Le big data du détail**, c'est ce qui se passe quand on conserve toutes ces données.

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: Une chaîne nationale génère des milliards de lignes de transactions par an, et en combinant celles-ci avec les identifiants de cartes de fidélité, la météo, les promotions et la navigation web, les analystes peuvent répondre à des questions qu'un seul directeur de magasin ne peut pas : quels produits se vendent ensemble, combien un changement de prix déplace vraiment le volume, quel magasin risque de tomber à court d'un article ce week-end.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: L'idée qui relie tout cela est la **précision d'inventaire** — à quel point le nombre dans l'ordinateur correspond au nombre sur l'étagère.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: Les détaillants trouvent régulièrement une précision de 60 à 80 % au niveau des articles individuels quand ils s'appuient uniquement sur les données du POS, car le vol, les articles mal placés et les erreurs de réception faussent silencieusement le compte.

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: Les mauvais comptages causent des **ruptures de stock** (vous pensez que vous l'avez, alors vous ne réapprovisionnez pas) et des **réductions excessives** (vous pensez que vous en êtes à court, alors vous surcommandez).

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: Presque tout dans ce domaine vise à combler cet écart.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la Vie Quotidienne

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: Entrez dans une Target aux États-Unis

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: et prenez un T-shirt à $24.99.

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: Le T-shirt a une étiquette de prix en papier avec une puce RFID laminée à l'intérieur.

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: Pendant la nuit, ou pendant un quart de travail lent, un associé balaye le rayon avec un lecteur portatif et lit chaque étiquette — y compris les trois T-shirts qu'un client a jetés au rayon des chaussettes, que le système avait compté comme « en stock » mais que nul client ne trouverait jamais.

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: C'est une **rupture de stock fantôme** : l'inventaire que l'ordinateur dit que tu as et que le client dit que tu n'as pas.

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: À la caisse, le scan du code-barres retire le T-shirt de l'inventaire disponible et, si vous avez scanné l'app Target Circle, associe l'achat à votre foyer.

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: Cet enregistrement alimente plusieurs systèmes en parallèle : le réapprovisionnement décide si le centre de distribution de Chicago livre plus de tailles médiums à ce magasin ; l'équipe de tarification voit si la promo a réellement augmenté les unités vendues ou juste fourni une réduction aux clients qui auraient payé le prix fort ; et le moteur de personnalisation note la catégorie pour les coupons que vous recevrez la semaine prochaine.

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: La même infrastructure alimente l'achat en ligne avec retrait en magasin.

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: Quand le site web promet « Prêt en 2 heures », il parie sur le fait que le dossier d'inventaire du magasin est exact.

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: Si le comptage est mauvais, la commande est annulée des heures plus tard et cela ébranle la confiance du client — ce qui est précisément la raison pour laquelle les chaînes ont beaucoup investi dans le RFID pour les catégories où cela se rentabilise.

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: Une mise en garde honnête : les balises RFID coûtent environ quelques centimes chacune, plus les lecteurs et les logiciels.

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: C'est facile à justifier pour un T-shirt à $25 avec des centaines de combinaisons taille-couleur, et difficile à justifier pour une boîte de soupe à 99 cents.

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi la confection l'a adopté en premier et le secteur alimentaire ne l'a pas vraiment fait.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en Trois Lignes

segments.src: 1. POS turns each checkout into a priced, timestamped, inventory-adjusting record — the base layer of all retail data.
segments.tr: 1. Le POS transforme chaque passage à la caisse en un enregistrement tarifié, horodaté et d'ajustement d'inventaire — la couche de base de toutes les données de détail.

segments.src: 2. RFID adds item-level, no-line-of-sight visibility, which mainly buys you inventory accuracy and therefore fewer out-of-stocks.
segments.tr: 2. Le RFID ajoute une visibilité au niveau des articles sans ligne de vue, ce qui apporte principalement une précision d'inventaire et donc moins de ruptures de stock.

segments.src: 3. Big data is the payoff layer: combining transactions with customer, price, and context data to decide what to stock, charge, and promote.
segments.tr: 3. Le big data est la couche de retour sur investissement : combiner les transactions avec les données client, de prix et de contexte pour décider quoi stocker, à quel prix et quoi promouvoir.

in.title: [Retailing 101 #14] Bip Kasir yang Menjalankan Seluruh Toko

segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > Setiap pemindaian, ketukan, dan pembacaan tag adalah titik data — dan ritel modern berjalan bergantung pada sebaik apa rantai mengubah titik-titik tersebut menjadi keputusan tentang apa yang harus stok, harga, dan pesan kembali.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: Sebuah **sistem informasi ritel** adalah infrastruktur yang memindahkan data dari lantai penjualan ke orang-orang yang membuat keputusan.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: Ini memiliki tiga lapisan yang layak diketahui.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS (point of sale)** adalah kasir.

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: Ketika kasir memindai kotak sereal, UPC barcode dicari di file item toko, yang mengembalikan deskripsi dan harga saat ini.

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: Satu pemindaian itu melakukan beberapa pekerjaan sekaligus: ia menentukan harga item, mencatat penjualan, mengurangi hitungan inventaris di tangan, dan memberi stempel waktu pada transaksi.

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: Inilah mengapa kasir mengetahui harga dan tag rak tidak perlu — desain yang disebut *price look-up*, standar di AS.

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: grocery sejak tahun 1970an.

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** melangkah lebih jauh.

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: Tag RFID adalah chip dan antena kecil, biasanya tanpa baterai, yang pembaca hidupkan dari jarak jauh dan baca secara nirkabel.

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: Keuntungan dibandingkan barcode: tidak perlu garis pandang, ratusan tag dibaca per detik, dan setiap tag membawa nomor seri unik untuk unit tertentu itu — bukan hanya "size M blue polo" tetapi *that one* size M blue polo.

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: Pengecer pakaian menggunakannya secara luas untuk perhitungan inventaris; seorang asosiasi toko dapat berjalan di lantai dengan pembaca genggam dan menghitung seluruh toko dalam waktu kurang dari satu jam daripada sepanjang malam.

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **Big data ritel** adalah apa yang terjadi ketika Anda menyimpan semuanya.

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: Rantai nasional menghasilkan miliaran baris transaksi per tahun, dan menggabungkan itu dengan ID kartu loyalitas, cuaca, promosi, dan penjelajahan web memungkinkan analis menjawab pertanyaan yang tidak dapat dijawab oleh seorang manajer toko: produk mana yang terjual bersama, berapa banyak perubahan harga yang benar-benar menggerakkan volume, toko mana yang akan kehabisan item akhir pekan ini.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: Ide penghubung adalah **akurasi inventaris** — seberapa dekat angka di komputer cocok dengan angka di rak.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: Pengecer secara rutin menemukan akurasi dalam kisaran 60–80% pada tingkat item individual ketika mereka mengandalkan data POS saja, karena pencurian, item yang salah tempat, dan kesalahan penerimaan semua mematahkan hitungan secara diam-diam.

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: Hitungan buruk menyebabkan **out-of-stocks** (Anda pikir Anda memilikinya, jadi Anda tidak memesan ulang) dan penurunan harga berlebihan (Anda pikir Anda habis, jadi Anda memesan berlebihan).

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: Hampir semua hal di bidang ini ditujukan untuk menutup kesenjangan itu.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Walk into a Target in the U.S.
segments.tr: Masuk ke Target di AS.

segments.src: and pick up a $24.99 T-shirt.
segments.tr: dan angkat T-shirt $24.99.

segments.src: The shirt has a paper price tag with an RFID chip laminated inside.
segments.tr: Kemeja memiliki label harga kertas dengan chip RFID berlapis di dalamnya.

segments.src: Overnight, or during a slow shift, an associate sweeps the department with a handheld reader and picks up every tag — including the three shirts a customer dumped in the sock aisle, which the system had counted as "in stock" but which no shopper would ever find.
segments.tr: Semalam, atau selama shift lambat, seorang asosiasi menyapu departemen dengan pembaca genggam dan mengambil setiap tag — termasuk tiga kemeja yang pelanggan buang di lorong kaus kaki, yang sistem telah menghitung sebagai "in stock" tetapi yang tidak akan pernah ditemukan oleh pembeli.

segments.src: That's a **phantom out-of-stock**: inventory the computer says you have and the customer says you don't.
segments.tr: Itu adalah **phantom out-of-stock**: inventaris yang komputer katakan Anda miliki dan pelanggan katakan Anda tidak.

segments.src: At checkout, the barcode scan drops the shirt out of on-hand inventory and, if you scanned the Target Circle app, ties the purchase to your household.
segments.tr: Saat checkout, pemindaian barcode mengeluarkan kemeja dari inventaris di tangan dan, jika Anda memindai aplikasi Target Circle, mengikat pembelian ke rumah tangga Anda.

segments.src: That record feeds several systems in parallel: replenishment decides whether the distribution center in Chicago ships more mediums to this store; the pricing team sees whether the promo actually lifted units or just gave a discount to people who'd have paid full price; and the personalization engine notes the category for the coupons you get next week.
segments.tr: Rekam itu memberi makan beberapa sistem secara paralel: pengisian kembali memutuskan apakah pusat distribusi di Chicago mengirim lebih banyak mediums ke toko ini; tim penetapan harga melihat apakah promosi benar-benar mengangkat unit atau hanya memberikan diskon kepada orang-orang yang akan membayar harga penuh; dan mesin personalisasi mencatat kategori untuk kupon yang Anda dapatkan minggu depan.

segments.src: The same infrastructure powers buy-online-pickup-in-store.
segments.tr: Infrastruktur yang sama mendayai buy-online-pickup-in-store.

segments.src: When the website promises "Ready in 2 hours," it is making a bet on the store's inventory record being right.
segments.tr: Ketika situs web menjanjikan "Ready in 2 hours," itu membuat taruhan pada catatan inventaris toko yang benar.

segments.src: If the count is wrong, the order gets canceled hours later and the customer's trust takes the hit — which is precisely why chains have spent so much on RFID for the categories where it pencils out.
segments.tr: Jika hitungan salah, pesanan dibatalkan jam kemudian dan kepercayaan pelanggan terkena dampak — yang persis mengapa rantai telah menghabiskan begitu banyak pada RFID untuk kategori di mana itu menguntungkan.

segments.src: One honest caveat: RFID tags cost roughly a few cents each, plus readers and software.
segments.tr: Satu peringatan jujur: tag RFID biaya kira-kira beberapa sen masing-masing, plus pembaca dan perangkat lunak.

segments.src: That's easy to justify on a $25 shirt with hundreds of size-color combinations, and hard to justify on a 99-cent can of soup.
segments.tr: Itu mudah untuk dibenarkan pada kemeja $25 dengan ratusan kombinasi ukuran-warna, dan sulit untuk dibenarkan pada kaleng sup 99-sen.

segments.src: This is why apparel adopted it first and grocery mostly hasn't.
segments.tr: Inilah mengapa pakaian mengadopsinya terlebih dahulu dan grocery sebagian besar belum.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. POS turns each checkout into a priced, timestamped, inventory-adjusting record — the base layer of all retail data.
segments.tr: 1. POS mengubah setiap checkout menjadi catatan yang dihargai, dicap waktu, penyesuaian inventaris — lapisan dasar semua data ritel.

segments.src: 2. RFID adds item-level, no-line-of-sight visibility, which mainly buys you inventory accuracy and therefore fewer out-of-stocks.
segments.tr: 2. RFID menambahkan visibilitas tingkat item, tanpa garis pandang, yang terutama membeli Anda akurasi inventaris dan karenanya lebih sedikit out-of-stocks.

segments.src: 3. Big data is the payoff layer: combining transactions with customer, price, and context data to decide what to stock, charge, and promote.
segments.tr: 3. Big data adalah lapisan imbal: menggabungkan transaksi dengan data pelanggan, harga, dan konteks untuk memutuskan apa yang harus stok, beban, dan promosi.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: 小売業者がPOSデータのみに依存する場合、個別商品レベルで60～80%の範囲の精度を日常的に見つけます。盗難、紛失商品、受け取りエラーはすべて数値を静かに破損させるからです。

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **POS (point of sale):** The system at checkout that prices items, captures the transaction, and updates inventory in one step.
segments.tr: - **POS（販売時点）：** チェックアウト時のシステムで、商品に価格をつけ、トランザクションをキャプチャし、在庫を1段階で更新します。

segments.src: - **UPC / barcode:** A printed code identifying a product type; it's a key into a database, not a container of price information.
segments.tr: - **UPC/バーコード：** 製品タイプを識別する印刷コード。それはデータベースへのキーであり、価格情報のコンテナーではありません。

segments.src: - **RFID:** Wireless tag-and-reader technology that identifies individual items without line of sight, at high speed.
segments.tr: - **RFID：** 無線タグおよびリーダーテクノロジーで、視線なしに個別商品を高速で識別します。

segments.src: - **Inventory accuracy:** The match rate between recorded on-hand quantity and actual physical quantity, measured per item.
segments.tr: - **在庫精度：** 記録された手持ち数量と実際の物理数量の一致率、商品ごとに測定されます。

segments.src: - **Out-of-stock (OOS):** A product a customer wants to buy but can't find available; "phantom" OOS means the system wrongly believes it's in stock.
segments.tr: - **欠品（OOS）：** 顧客が購入したいが、利用可能な商品が見つからない場合。「幻」のOOSはシステムが誤って在庫があると信じることを意味します。

segments.src: - **Shrinkage:** Inventory lost to theft, damage, or error — a main reason recorded counts drift away from reality.
segments.tr: - **目減り：** 盗難、損傷、またはエラーによって失われた在庫。記録された数が現実から離れる主な理由です。

de.title: [Einzelhandel 101 #14] Der Kassierer-Piep, der den ganzen Laden steuert

segments.src: > Every scan, tap, and tag read is a data point — and modern retail runs on how well a chain turns those points into decisions about what to stock, price, and reorder.
segments.tr: > Jeder Scan, jeder Tipp und jeder Tag-Read ist ein Datenpunkt — und moderner Einzelhandel läuft darauf, wie gut eine Kette diese Punkte in Entscheidungen darüber umwandelt, was zu lagern, zu preisen und nachzubestellen ist.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heute's Konzept

segments.src: A **retail information system** is the plumbing that moves data from the sales floor to the people who make decisions.
segments.tr: Ein **Einzelhandels-Informationssystem** ist die Infrastruktur, die Daten vom Verkaufsort zu den Entscheidungsträgern transportiert.

segments.src: It has three layers worth knowing.
segments.tr: Es hat drei Schichten, die man kennen sollte.

segments.src: **POS (point of sale)** is the register.
segments.tr: **POS (Verkaufsstelle)** ist die Kasse.

segments.src: When a cashier scans a box of cereal, the barcode's UPC is looked up in the store's item file, which returns the description and the current price.
segments.tr: Wenn ein Kassierer eine Schachtel Getreide scannt, wird der UPC des Barcodes in der Artikeldatei des Geschäfts nachgeschlagen, die die Beschreibung und den aktuellen Preis zurückgibt.

segments.src: That one scan does several jobs at once: it prices the item, records the sale, decrements the on-hand inventory count, and timestamps the transaction.
segments.tr: Dieser eine Scan erledigt mehrere Aufgaben auf einmal: Er preist den Artikel, erfasst den Verkauf, vermindert den verfügbaren Bestand und zeitstempelt die Transaktion.

segments.src: This is why the register knows the price and the shelf tag doesn't have to — a design called *price look-up*, standard in U.S.
segments.tr: Deshalb kennt die Kasse den Preis und das Regaletikett nicht — ein Design namens *Preisabfrage*, Standard in den USA.

segments.src: grocery since the 1970s.
segments.tr: Lebensmittelhandel seit den 1970er Jahren.

segments.src: **RFID (radio frequency identification)** goes a step further.
segments.tr: **RFID (Radiofrequenz-Identifikation)** geht einen Schritt weiter.

segments.src: An RFID tag is a tiny chip and antenna, usually with no battery, that a reader powers up from a distance and reads wirelessly.
segments.tr: Ein RFID-Tag ist ein kleiner Chip und eine Antenne, normalerweise ohne Batterie, den ein Lesegerät aus der Ferne mit Strom versorgt und drahtlos liest.

segments.src: The advantages over barcodes: no line of sight needed, hundreds of tags read per second, and each tag carries a serial number unique to that specific unit — not just "size M blue polo" but *that one* size M blue polo.
segments.tr: Die Vorteile gegenüber Barcodes: keine Sichtlinie erforderlich, Hunderte von Tags pro Sekunde lesbar, und jedes Tag trägt eine Seriennummer, die eindeutig für diese spezifische Einheit ist — nicht nur "Größe M blaues Polo", sondern *dieses* Größe M blaue Polo.

segments.src: Apparel retailers use it heavily for inventory counts; a store associate can walk the floor with a handheld reader and count the whole store in under an hour instead of a full night.
segments.tr: Einzelhändler für Bekleidung nutzen es intensiv für Bestandszählungen; ein Verkäufer kann mit einem tragbaren Lesegerät über den Boden gehen und den ganzen Laden in unter einer Stunde statt einer ganzen Nacht zählen.

segments.src: **Retail big data** is what happens when you keep all of it.
segments.tr: **Einzelhandels-Big-Data** ist das, was passiert, wenn man alles speichert.

segments.src: A national chain generates billions of transaction lines a year, and combining those with loyalty-card IDs, weather, promotions, and web browsing lets analysts answer questions a single store manager can't: which products sell together, how much a price change actually moves volume, which store is about to run out of an item this weekend.
segments.tr: Eine nationale Kette generiert jedes Jahr Milliarden von Transaktionszeilen, und die Kombination dieser mit Kundenkarten-IDs, Wetter, Promotionen und Browsing-Verhalten ermöglicht es Analysten, Fragen zu beantworten, die ein einzelner Geschäftsführer nicht kann: welche Produkte zusammen verkauft werden, wie viel eine Preisänderung tatsächlich das Volumen beeinflusst, welcher Laden dieses Wochenende bald einen Artikel ausverkauft hat.

segments.src: The connecting idea is **inventory accuracy** — how closely the number in the computer matches the number on the shelf.
segments.tr: Die verbindende Idee ist **Bestandsgenauigkeit** — wie genau die Zahl im Computer mit der Zahl im Regal übereinstimmt.

segments.src: Retailers routinely find accuracy in the 60–80% range at the individual item level when they rely on POS data alone, because theft, misplaced items, and receiving errors all break the count silently.
segments.tr: Einzelhändler finden routinemäßig Genauigkeit im Bereich von 60–80% auf Artikel-Ebene, wenn sie sich nur auf POS-Daten verlassen, denn Diebstahl, fehlplatzierte Artikel und Empfangsfehler beeinflussen die Zählung still und leise.

segments.src: Bad counts cause **out-of-stocks** (you think you have it, so you don't reorder) and excess markdowns (you think you're out, so you over-order).
segments.tr: Schlechte Zählungen verursachen **Ausverkauft-Situationen** (man denkt, es ist vorhanden, also bestellt man nicht nach) und übermäßige Preisreduktionen (man denkt, es ist weg, also bestellt man zu viel).

segments.src: Nearly everything in this field is aimed at closing that gap.
segments.tr: Beinahe alles in diesem Bereich zielt darauf ab, diese Lücke zu schließen.
